headlines.title: 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan takes blame for the crash that left him with a concussion
headlines.description: San Francisco 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan took the blame for the car crash that left him with a concussion and other injuries, saying he took his eyes off the road to reach for his fallen cell phone before hitting another vehicle. Shanahan crashed into a 21-year-old woman driving in the other direction in Palo Alto on July 14 and was left with a concussion, broken ribs, a broken nose and broken left hand and stitches for a large cut above his right eye. Shanahan was briefly hospitalized following the crash and hasn’t been able to coach the team at the start of training camp. The other driver suffered minor injuries and did not need to be hospitalized. Shanahan spoke to a small group of reporters on Tuesday for the first time since the crash to explain what happened from his vantage point and to make clear the crash was his fault. “I was going 20 miles an hour,” Shanahan said. “I was not on my phone, but I dropped my phone, and it was stuck in my seats. It was on my lap, and it slid off, and I went down to look for it, and took my eyes off the road for two seconds, and as I was coming up, the air bags hit me in my face.” Police filed no charges in the crash. Palo Alto police Lt. Nicholas Martinez confirmed Shanahan’s version of the crash was correct and that a mistake in a report transmitted to a state database incorrectly blamed the crash on the other driver. “I can confirm that Kyle Shanahan’s statement that he provided is correct and that he was found at fault for the collision,” Martinez said in a statement Tuesday. “There was a clerical error in the preparation of the report that was transmitted to the state database. We are in the process of correcting that error. It is the officer’s discretion at the scene of the collision as to whether they issue a citation to either party. It is not uncommon for officers to elect to not issue a citation to either party involved in a collision. Neither party in this situation was provided preferential treatment.” Shanahan has been unable to run the team or practice since training camp started on Saturday with assistant Chris Foerster in charge with assistance from coordinators Raheem Morris, Klay Kubiak and Brant Boyer. Shanahan has come out for portions of the first two practices to watch alongside general manager John Lynch. He said he is not bothered by the sunlight but loud noises like the music at practice are still an issue. Shanahan said he has made considerable progress and expects to make a full recovery. The 49ers have said that Shanahan is going through a similar protocol to the one used for players after a concussion and will resume coaching when he is recovered. Shanahan is entering his 10th season as 49ers coach and is one of the most highly regarded coaches in the game for his offensive acumen. San Francisco has made two trips to the Super Bowl under his watch following the 2019 and 2023 seasons and made two additional appearances in the NFC title game in the 2021 and ’22 seasons. Shanahan has a 91-72 record in the regular season and playoffs for the 49ers, ranking third in franchise history in wins behind George Seifert (108) and Bill Walsh (102). The team overcame significant injuries last season to finish 12-5 in the regular season and win a playoff game as Shanahan finished fifth in voting for the AP NFL Coach of the Year. ___ AP NFL: https://apnews.com/NFL

headlines.title: ‘He deserves it!' Santa Cruz lifeguard who saved boy to receive high honor, Trump says
headlines.description: A teenage lifeguard who saved a boy from rough surf in Santa Cruz will be welcomed to the White House to receive recognition for the rescue, President Donald Trump said Tuesday. The dramatic water rescue at Seabright Beach last weekend was caught on video. The footage showed the 16-year-old lifeguard holding onto the boy and keeping his head afloat as they were battered by wave after wave. The lifeguard, along with a counterpart, eventually managed to get the boy back on dry ground. “We’re going to bring this heroic young man, and his family, into the White House with, perhaps, the boy he saved, to give him a High Civilian Honor,” Trump said in a post on social media. “Very brave, he deserves it!” Trump’s son Eric said the lifeguard should be presented with the “highest civilian honor.” Witness Scott Vander Dussen said the waves were coming in at a normal cadence and intensity before everything escalated. “It changed in a heartbeat,” he said. “It caught a lot of people off guard. Unfortunately, this young man was overwhelmed and swept out in just a moment’s time.” After being rescued, the boy was evaluated by paramedics before being released to his parents, Vander Dussen said. “I’m glad it ended the way that it did,” he said. “I’m certain that if the lifeguards weren’t there, he wouldn’t have gone home that night.”

headlines.title: Draymond Green agrees to Warriors return on one-year, $27.7M contract, per agent
headlines.description: Draymond Green is back. Green has agreed to return to the Warriors on a one-year, $27.7 million contract, his agent Rich Paul told ESPN’s Shams Charania on Tuesday morning. Earlier this offseason, Green declined his $27.7 million player option to become a free agent and give Golden State flexibility to pursue LeBron James in NBA free agency. But with James choosing the Philadelphia 76ers, the Warriors made sure to secure their guy. In 14 seasons, Green has averaged 8.7 points, 6.8 rebounds and 5.6 assists through 949 games and 794 starts. Green now will play his 15th consecutive season in the Bay, where he’s won four NBA championships and continues to chase a fifth. headlines.title: Bay Area braces for weekend heat as fire danger, beach hazards persist
headlines.description: Warm weather will gradually build across the Bay Area this week, with inland communities facing increasing heat and elevated fire weather concerns, and dangerous beach conditions will persist even with cooler temperatures near the coast. In an early Tuesday morning advisory, the National Weather Service said breezy onshore winds will continue each afternoon and evening through the middle of the week, helping keep coastal areas relatively mild while inland temps climb. Moderate HeatRisk is expected to develop across many interior locations beginning Thursday and continue into the weekend. Forecasters said the hottest days are expected on Saturday and Sunday, when interior parts of the North Bay, East Bay and South Bay could see highs in the upper 80s to near 100 degrees. Interior Monterey County is forecast to be even hotter, reaching the 90s to near 110 degrees, with some areas facing major to extreme HeatRisk over the weekend. Fire danger will also remain elevated through midweek across the Diablo Range, Santa Lucia Range and other inland areas because of hot temps, low daytime humidity, breezy afternoon winds and only limited overnight moisture recovery. The weather service urged residents to avoid activities that could spark a wildfire, including leaving campfires unattended or dragging chains behind vehicles. Along California’s Pacific coast, hazardous beach conditions are expected to continue through at least Saturday, with an increased risk of sneaker waves and strong rip currents. Forecasters urged beachgoers to stay off jetties, piers and rocks, remain out of the water if surf becomes dangerous, and never turn their backs on the ocean.

headlines.title: 3 dead in separate weekend collisions near Gilroy
headlines.description: Three people died in separate vehicle crashes over the weekend in Santa Clara County, California Highway Patrol officials said. The first was a 45-year-old woman from Watsonville who was riding a Honda motorcycle on Highway 101 near the Sargent Bridge overcrossing south of Gilroy at about 5:10 p.m. Saturday when she crashed for an unknown reason, according to the CHP. The woman, whose name was not immediately released, died at the scene. The second was a 34-year-old San Jose man who was riding a Harley-Davidson motorcycle when he crashed into a Chevrolet Silverado towing a trailer on State Route 152 near Ferguson Road east of Gilroy at about 2:40 p.m. Saturday, according to the CHP. The man, whose name was not immediately released, died at the scene. The third fatality was a 56-year-old man from Aptos. He was driving a Toyota pickup on Bolsa Road north of Bloomfield Road when it collided head-on with a Ford F150 at about 4:35 p.m. Sunday, according to the CHP. The Toyota driver died at the scene. The Ford driver was arrested for allegedly trying to run from the area on foot, CHP officials said. Anyone with information about any of these fatalities is asked to call the CHP Hollister-Gilroy Area office at 408-427-0700.

headlines.title: Red Cross requests blood donations to address crisis
headlines.description: The American Red Cross has declared an emergency blood shortage this summer for only the second time in the 145-year history of the organization. They issued an urgent request nationwide for donations on Monday, asking people, including Bay Area residents, to book appointments to donate blood soon. All blood types are needed, especially type O blood, which is under limited distribution to hospitals because the nonprofit currently has less than a one-day supply on hand. The Red Cross supplies about 40% of the nation’s blood to hospitals and healthcare facilities for surgeries, cancer treatment, chronic illnesses and traumatic injuries. “If just three more donors gave at each blood drive this summer, we could help the blood supply rebound and ensure hospitals have the blood products they need throughout the remainder of the season,” said Paul Sullivan, a spokesperson for donor services at the Red Cross. The Red Cross said thousands of people have donated since the emergency was announced earlier in July, but donations still aren’t keeping up with hospital demand. Extreme heat, poor air quality and widespread foodborne illnesses are contributing to lower donor turnout this summer, according to the nonprofit. There are many upcoming opportunities to donate blood across Alameda, Contra Costa, San Francisco and Santa Clara counties. Appointments can be booked using the Blood Donor App, by visiting RedCrossBlood.org or calling 1-800-RED-CROSS. As a thank you, donors who give blood by July 31 will receive a Fandango movie ticket. In August, the Red Cross will instead offer donors a $20 Amazon gift card.

headlines.title: Third victim identified in San Francisco Bay capsized boat tragedy
headlines.description: The third person found dead after a boat capsized July 14 in the San Francisco Bay has been identified by the Medical Examiner’s Office. Carol Boisa, 74, of Sacramento County, was identified by the San Francisco Medical Examiner’s Office after being found west of the Golden Gate Bridge this weekend. On Saturday at approximately 10 a.m., San Francisco police officers said a person was found dead near Point Diablo on the Marin County side of the Golden Gate channel. Out of the 20 passengers attending a memorial service aboard the 49-foot cabin cruiser, three people and one dog have been pronounced dead. One more person remains missing. The San Francisco Medical Examiner’s Office identified Clifford Boisa, 79, of Sutter County, as the first victim confirmed dead. Clifford was initially rescued from the water when the boat capsized but later was pronounced dead after succumbing to his injuries. On July 16, just two days after the vessel sank, an SFPD marine unit recovered another body in the water west of Treasure Island. The Medical Examiner’s Office identified the individual as Tondra Miller, a 58-year-old woman from Sacramento County. Authorities believe that many of the people who perished in the sinking may have initially been trapped inside the vessel’s enclosed main or lower deck, said U.S. Coast Guard Capt. Jarod Toczko. At survivor debriefings shortly after the rescue, passengers told the Coast Guard that people were in the enclosed decks when the boat was sailing. On July 17, the sunken vessel was located by the SFPD marine unit using boat-mounted sonar technology. Police are currently continuing to assess the wreckage and feasibility of possibly recovering or lifting the vessel to the surface. San Francisco Jul 16 Investigative Unit Jul 22 San Francisco Jul 16 2 of 3 missing from capsized boat in San Francisco Bay identified

headlines.title: 1 dead, 6 injured in mass shooting at pop-up party near Morgan Hill
headlines.description: Detectives are searching for answers and asking witnesses to come forward after a deadly mass shooting at a pop-up birthday party near Morgan Hill left one person dead and six others injured over the weekend. Family members identified the person killed as Desi Romero, known to loved ones as “Pepper.” An online fundraiser created to help pay for funeral expenses described Romero as a cherished son, brother, grandson, cousin and friend who had a way of bringing joy to everyone around him. “Pepper was taken from us far too soon, and our hearts are shattered,” the family wrote in the fundraiser. His grandfather noted that Romero once played for Evergreen Little League. In a statement, an acquaintance from his Little League days remembered him fondly. “He was a pleasure to watch on the field… and was always one of the most talented players — if not the most talented player — on the field,” the statement read. The unsanctioned Saturday night party was hosted by a Bay Area streamer in a field in an unincorporated area near Morgan Hill. Investigators estimate about 300 people attended the event. “This was sort of a pop-up party that was advertised on social media,” said Brooks Jarosz of the Santa Clara County Sheriff’s Office. “The location of that party was not given out until hours before the event occurred.” One woman who attended the party told NBC Bay Area there was security present and that men were being patted down before entering. However, she said one man somehow got past security with a handgun. “The guy who had the gun snuck in,” the woman said. “I don’t know how he did. Everyone saw that he had a gun, and then he got mad.” What was supposed to be a birthday celebration quickly ended in tragedy when gunfire erupted. Along with Romero’s death, six others suffered gunshot wounds. “For some it was the stomach, one in the ankle, one in the shoulder,” Jarosz said. “I can report now that four of the six who were injured are still in the hospital.” The sheriff’s office confirmed the shooter used a handgun, but investigators have not yet said whether they believe the shooting was targeted or if there is any gang connection. While investigators have already interviewed more than a dozen people, they are urging many more to come forward to help piece together what led up to the violence. “We want to talk to more so we can see if all of those stories match up and get a clear understanding of what happened,” Jarosz said. Authorities are asking anyone who attended the party, or who has photos or video from that night, to contact the Santa Clara County Sheriff’s Office.

headlines.title: Sushi Confidential reportedly closing San Pedro Square location
headlines.description: Sushi Confidential is closing its downtown San Jose location in San Pedro Square despite a successful run during the FIFA World Cup. The restaurant’s owner told the Mercury News that the decision to close was made before the recent World Cup matches, which drew large crowds to San Pedro Square. The restaurant’s last day is scheduled for Aug. 30. According to the owner, the focus will shift to Sushi Confidential’s three other San Jose locations, as well as its restaurants in Campbell and Morgan Hill. Employees affected by the closure will be relocated. The owner also said the restaurant taking over the space is interested in keeping the current staff.

headlines.title: Lawmakers push for national safety standards for autonomous vehicles
headlines.description: As more Waymos and other autonomous vehicles hit the road, a California congressman and the mayor of San Francisco are calling for new national safety standards. Congressman Kevin Mullin, San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie, the city’s fire chief and advocates for highway and auto safety gathered in San Francisco on Tuesday to urge the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration to establish uniform safety standards across state lines. The group says there is growing evidence that autonomous vehicles are creating dangerous situations and interfering with first responders during power outages and other emergencies. The officials are asking the federal agency to develop consistent safety regulations for autonomous vehicles nationwide. NBC Bay Area’s Kris Sanchez has the full report in the video above.

headlines.title: 49ers' Kyle Shanahan clarifies car accident details, says crash was his fault
headlines.description: SANTA CLARA — Kyle Shanahan on Tuesday wanted to clear up some things. Public records indicated that Shanahan, the 49ers’ head coach, was not at fault for the two-car collision on July 14 in Palo Alto. Shanahan revealed that the report was inaccurate. “I was going 20 miles an hour,” Shanahan said. “I was not on my phone, but I dropped my phone, and it was stuck in my seats. It was on my lap, and it slid off, and I went down to look for it, and took my eyes off the road for two seconds, and as I was coming up, the airbags hit me in my face.” The two vehicles, Shanahan’s black 2023 Tesla Model S and the other driver’s blue 2025 Mercedes-Benz GLC 300, collided at Alma Street and Hamilton Avenue in Palo Alto. Shanahan was heading south on Alma, while the other driver was headed northbound on Alma. Shanahan said he was upset that the other driver, identified in the report as a 21-year-old female, was blamed for making an unsafe turn. “I hit her,” Shanahan said. “I don’t know why it was reported that way.” Jeremy Jones, the 49ers’ vice president of security operations, said the inaccurate version of events was the result of a clerical error that is being corrected on the California Crash Reporting System database. “It just crushed me that the (other driver) gets blamed for it,” said Shanahan, adding that he has nothing to hide and just wanted to set the record straight. Authorities reported that neither drugs nor alcohol had any role in the accident, which occurred at 6:14 p.m. The other driver was not injured in the crash, Palo Alto police told ESPN. Shanahan, meanwhile, sustained a concussion, as well as a broken nose, ribs and left hand. The airbag deployed, which broke his nose, and he likely received the V-shaped gash near his right eye from the visor. Shanahan said he did not sustain a “severe concussion,” which is a medical term that involves a loss of consciousness and amnesia. “I did not have amnesia,” Shanahan said. “I don’t have amnesia. I remember the wreck, and I never got knocked out.” Shanahan said he asked to remain at the scene of the accident until his wife, Mandy, arrived. He was transported to Stanford Hospital. He was in the hospital for eight to 10 hours and underwent plastic surgery. Shanahan, 46, enters his 10th season as 49ers head coach. While he continues to deal with the lasting effects of his concussion, he is on a limited schedule as the 49ers opened training camp over the weekend. Assistant head coach Chris Foerster is taking on the role as the 49ers’ front man. Shanahan spent time on the practice field during 11-on-11 drills on Sunday and Monday. Shanahan did not place any timetable on his return to full head-coaching duties. He continues to battle his emotions from his role in such a traumatic event, as he makes slow progress in his recovery from his head injury. “I’m so much better,” he said. “I know I’m going to be all right.” Download and follow the 49ers Talk Podcast This story originally appeared on NBCSportsBayArea.com.

headlines.title: What local authorities believe led to 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan's car accident
headlines.description: New details surrounding 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan’s recent car accident have emerged. The San Francisco coach was involved in a head-on collision with another driver on July 14 in Palo Alto, CA and, as NBC Sports Bay Area’s Matt Maiocco reported Saturday, suffered numerous injuries, including a concussion, broken ribs, a broken nose and a broken hand. Public records from the California Crash Reporting System, a statewide database of collisions, show the accident occurred at 6:12 p.m. PT at Alma Street and Hamilton Avenue after a 21-year-old woman made an unsafe turn while driving a Mercedes SUV in the opposite direction on a four-lane, 25-mph street. (h/t the San Francisco Chronicle’s Noah Furtado and Eric Branch) Shanahan was driving south on Alma Street, while the other driver was headed north. The records also show that Shanahan was holding and using a cellphone at the time, which authorities listed as a factor in the accident, but stated that he was not at fault for the wreck. According to the database, neither Shanahan nor the woman were found to have been drinking, and both parties were wearing seat belts. Palo Alto police Lt. Nicholas Martinez told the San Francisco Chronicle on Saturday that the officers who responded to the accident did not issue any citations or suspect either driver of being impaired and that both parties remained at the scene and cooperated with police. Contrary to what Palo Alto police told ESPN, the database states both parties sustained injuries. Since the accident, Shanahan has returned to the 49ers’ facility and was on hand for the 11-on-11 portions of San Francisco’s first two training camp practices on Sunday and Monday. Assistant head coach Chris Foerster will take on some of Shanahan’s responsibilties in training camp until the head coach is cleared to return to his everyday role.
